professor.definition: A person who is a member of the faculty at a college or university.

lecturer.definition: A teacher who gives classes or lectures at a college or university.

teaching-assistant.definition: A helper who supports a teacher in the classroom.

dean.definition: The head of a faculty or school within a university.

chancellor.definition: The head or ceremonial leader of a university, depending on its system.

tutor.definition: A person who teaches or helps one student or a small group.

researcher.definition: A scientist who devotes themself to doing research.

postdoc.definition: A scholar or researcher who is involved in academic study beyond the level of a doctoral degree.

lecture.definition: A speech that is open to the public.

seminar.definition: A course offered for a small group of advanced students.

tutorial.definition: A session of intensive tuition given by a tutor to an individual or to a small number of students.

lab-session.definition: A scheduled class period in which students carry out practical experiments or laboratory work.
lab-session.exampleUsage: The lab session included a simple chemistry experiment.

workshop.definition: A brief intensive course for a small group.

syllabus.definition: A document listing a course's topics, requirements, and schedule.

prerequisite.definition: Something that is required in advance.

elective.definition: A course that a student can choose rather than one they must take.

core-course.definition: A course that anchors an academic curriculum by providing required or foundational learning.

credit-hour.definition: A measure of academic credit based on attending one class hour each week throughout a semester.

grade.definition: A mark or result showing how well work was done.

gpa.definition: A measure of a student's academic achievement at a college or university.

pass-fail.definition: A grading system that records only whether a student passed or failed, rather than giving a detailed grade.
pass-fail.exampleUsage: The short course is assessed on a pass/fail basis.

dean-s-list.definition: A published list of students who achieved very high academic results during a term.
dean-s-list.exampleUsage: Her strong grades placed her on the dean's list.

honor-roll.definition: A list of students officially recognized for high academic achievement.
honor-roll.exampleUsage: Several students were added to the honor roll.

transcript.definition: An official record of a student's courses and grades.

midterm.definition: An examination held around the middle of an academic term.

final-exam.definition: An examination at the end of a course or academic term measures students’ understanding of all the material.

quiz.definition: An examination consisting of a few short questions.

rubric.definition: A set of criteria used to assess a piece of work.

bachelor-s.definition: An undergraduate academic degree awarded after completing a university or college program.
bachelor-s.exampleUsage: She is studying for a bachelor's degree in engineering.

master-s.definition: A postgraduate academic degree usually earned after a bachelor's degree.
master-s.exampleUsage: He completed a master's degree in data science.

doctorate.definition: One of the highest earned academic degrees conferred by a university.

associate-s.definition: An undergraduate degree usually awarded after about two years of study at a college.
associate-s.exampleUsage: The college offers an associate's degree in business.

diploma.definition: A document certifying the successful completion of a course of study.

certificate.definition: A document confirming that someone has completed a course or earned a qualification.

major.definition: The main subject a student studies for a degree.

minor.definition: A secondary subject a student studies alongside a major.

double-major.definition: A course of study in which a student completes the main requirements for two academic subjects.
double-major.exampleUsage: She chose a double major in mathematics and economics.

concentration.definition: A focused area of study within a broader academic subject.
